blocks.text: The nature of cases in Russian is detailed more thoroughly on its dedicated page. A case tells you what a noun, pronoun, or adjective is doing in a sentence, and is denoted by a set of rules that change the end of the word.

For instance, if a person or thing is the object of a sentence (the 'object' is the thing which is being verbed), then you place it in the accusative case; an example of a rule for this case states that words which usually end in **а**, such as **книга** ('book'), change the **a** to **у** (so **книга** becomes **книгу**). English relies on the *order* of words to convey this kind of meaning, but Russian does this with grammatical cases, so they use word order for different purposes.

So, cases have rules that change a word and tell you what it's doing in a sentence. A word in the accusative case is the thing being verbed ('the dog chased *the cat**), the genitive case describes something being counted ('he has five *apples**) or something owned ('the house *of Sasha**, or **Sasha's* house'), and so on.
The nominative case is special, as there are few rules to learn. When you look up a word in the dictionary, it will be in its nominative form.

Thus, you don't need any rules to change a word into the nominative case: it's already in it by default. The only rules that are used in the nominative case are those to turn a word into its plural form (each case has its own rules for converting a word into the singular of that case, and into that case's plural form).
The nominative case is used when no other case is being used. Its use is to denote a word as being the *subject* of a verb - that is, the thing that's doing the verb.
For instance, in the sentence, "Peter is driving a car", 'Peter' is the *subject* of the verb 'to drive'. In Russian, then, the word 'Peter' would be placed in the nominative case.
If you don't know what case to put a word in, use the nominative, and you'll probably be right.

One of the first things to learn in Russian is the idea of gender; this article will give a brief overview, but see the dedicated page for a more thorough treatment. Unlike French, where gender is arbitrary, you can work out a word's gender by its ending:

items: Most words are *MASCULINE*, and they end in a consonant in the nominative case: **б, в, г, д, ж, з, й к, л, м, н, п, р, с, т, ф, х, ч, ц, ш**, or **щ**. It is easiest to remember that a word that doesn't have a feminine or neuter ending is probably masculine, though you will soon learn to predict gender intuitively. Words which are masculine in meaning but feminine in grammar (such as 'uncle', **дядя**), are classed as masculine (for adjectives, pronouns, etc.), but conjugate as a feminine noun (**дядя >> дядю**, for instance). The soft sign, **ь**, can be on either masculine or feminine nouns. Examples of masculine nouns in the nominative case are **стул** ('chair'), **музей** ('museum'), and **медведь**' ('bear').
Most other words are *FEMININE*, and they end in **а** or **я**, or occasionally **ь**. Examples are **корова** ('cow'), **змея** ('snake'), and **дочь** ('daughter').
Then there are *NEUTER* words, which end in either **o** or **e**. Examples are **письмо** ('letter'), **море** ('sea'), and **платье** ('dress').

blocks.text: You may have noticed that not all the letters in the Russian alphabet have been used here, such as **ё**, **у**, **и**, etc. This is because they don't occur on the ends of default, nominative, singular nouns, and instead are really only used as noun endings after conjugation (**ы**, for instance, is the common *plural* ending for nouns). Rarely, unusual or foreign words may end in these non-standard letters, such as **такси** ('taxi') - these have irregular genders, and are indeclinable (that is, they don't change according to case or number).

Finally, apart from denoting verbal subjects and helping us tell a word's gender, the nominative has one other, small use: it is used after some prepositions. Like other cases, there are prepositions that call the nominative case, though these are extremely rare nowadays, and are mostly used in sayings and idioms. They are:

items: **За** + *nom*, 'of', 'what kind of' - this preposition is used in sentences like, "What kind of X is Y?", and are constructed in Russian using the word **что**: "Что Y за X", with both X and Y being in the nominative. For example: What kind of woman is she? **Что она за женщина?**. What kind of worker is Ivan? **Что Иван за работник?**.
**В** + *nom*, 'became' - this is used only with plural nouns to denote joining a group: "I became a worker", **Я в рабочие**.

items.text: The nominative case is the basic form in which nouns appear in dictionaries. The main functions of the nominative case are:
points: The nominative of the subject: *Студент читает. Студенты читают.*
The nominative of the predicate: *Мой брат — студент. Мои братья — студенты.*

Further sentences, so that every pattern above is practised: from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR), with their English.

exercises.q: ___ (мафия, nom. sg.) использует законные деловые операции как прикрытие.
exercises.prompt: The Mafia uses legitimate business operations as a front.
exercises.why: **мафия → мафия** (nom. sg.). Declines like армия. Nominative: the ending is -я.

exercises.q: ___ (родитель, nom. pl.) могут передать своему потомству множество заболеваний.
exercises.prompt: Parents can pass many diseases on to their offspring.
exercises.why: **родитель → родители** (nom. pl.). Declines like учитель. Ending -ь → -и.

exercises.q: ___ (террорист, nom. pl.) были повсюду.
exercises.prompt: Terrorists were everywhere.
exercises.why: **террорист → террористы** (nom. pl.). Declines like студент. Ending — (no ending) → -ы.

exercises.q: ___ (кот, nom. sg.) прижал нос к окну.
exercises.prompt: The cat pressed its nose against the window.
exercises.why: **кот → кот** (nom. sg.). Declines like студент. Nominative: the ending is — (no ending).

exercises.q: ___ (неприятель, nom. sg.) учинил ужасную бойню в городе.
exercises.prompt: The enemy committed a horrible slaughter in the city.
exercises.why: **неприятель → неприятель** (nom. sg.). Declines like учитель. Nominative: the ending is -ь.

exercises.q: ___ (птица, nom. sg.) попалась в силки.
exercises.prompt: The bird got caught in a snare.
exercises.why: **птица → птица** (nom. sg.). Declines like сестра. Nominative: the ending is -а.

exercises.q: ___ (синоптик, nom. pl.) обещают москвичам жаркое лето.
exercises.prompt: The weather forecasters are promising Muscovites a hot summer.
exercises.why: **синоптик → синоптики** (nom. pl.). Declines like студент. Ending — (no ending) → -и.

exercises.q: ___ (археолог, nom. sg.) изучает древнеримские развалины.
exercises.prompt: The archaeologist is studying old Roman ruins.
exercises.why: **археолог → археолог** (nom. sg.). Declines like студент. Nominative: the ending is — (no ending).

exercises.q: ___ (мой сын, nom. sg.) играет в футбол в спортклубе.
exercises.prompt: My son plays football in a sports club.
exercises.why: **сын → сын** (nom. sg.). Declines like студент. Nominative: the ending is — (no ending).  **мой → мой** (nom. sg. m., agreeing with сын). Declines like мой. Nominative: the ending is -й.

exercises.q: ___ (мой брат, nom. sg.) страдает аутизмом?
exercises.prompt: Does my brother suffer from autism?
exercises.why: **брат → брат** (nom. sg.). Declines like студент. Nominative: the ending is — (no ending).  **мой → мой** (nom. sg. m., agreeing with брат). Declines like мой. Nominative: the ending is -й.

exercises.q: ___ (ведьма, nom. sg.) бросила жабу в свой котёл.
exercises.prompt: The witch threw the toad into her cauldron.
exercises.why: **ведьма → ведьма** (nom. sg.). Declines like сестра. Nominative: the ending is -а.

exercises.q: ___ (гунтер, nom. sg.) вздохнул с досадой и беспокойством.
exercises.prompt: Gunter sighed with frustration and worry.
exercises.why: **гунтер → гунтер** (nom. sg.). Declines like студент. Nominative: the ending is — (no ending).

exercises.q: ___ (кувалда, nom. sg.) разбивает стекло, но куёт сталь.
exercises.prompt: A sledgehammer breaks glass but forges steel.
exercises.why: **кувалда → кувалда** (nom. sg.). Declines like газета. Nominative: the ending is -а.

exercises.q: ___ (блудный сын, nom. sg.) вернулся домой.
exercises.prompt: The prodigal son returned home.
exercises.why: **сын → сын** (nom. sg.). Declines like студент. Nominative: the ending is — (no ending).  **блудный → блудный** (nom. sg. m., agreeing with сын). Declines like новый. Nominative: the ending is -ый.

exercises.q: ___ (собака, nom. sg.) бежала за зайцем.
exercises.prompt: The dog ran after the rabbit.
exercises.why: **собака → собака** (nom. sg.). Declines like сестра. Nominative: the ending is -а.

exercises.q: ___ (кошка, nom. sg.) съела мою мышку.
exercises.prompt: A cat ate my mouse.
exercises.why: **кошка → кошка** (nom. sg.). Declines like сестра. Nominative: the ending is -а.

exercises.q: ___ (меланхолия, nom. sg.) питает безумие.
exercises.prompt: Melancholy is the nurse of frenzy.
exercises.why: **меланхолия → меланхолия** (nom. sg.). Declines like армия. Nominative: the ending is -я.

exercises.q: ___ (художница, nom. sg.) пишет картину.
exercises.prompt: The artist is painting a picture.
exercises.why: **художница → художница** (nom. sg.). Declines like сестра. Nominative: the ending is -а.

exercises.q: ___ (промокательная бумага, nom. sg.) впитывает чернила.
exercises.prompt: Blotting paper absorbs ink.
exercises.why: **бумага → бумага** (nom. sg.). Declines like газета. Nominative: the ending is -а.  **промокательный → промокательная** (nom. sg. f., agreeing with бумага). Declines like новый. Nominative: the ending is -ая.

exercises.q: ___ (мальчик, nom. sg.) получил нагоняй.
exercises.prompt: The boy got scolded.
exercises.why: **мальчик → мальчик** (nom. sg.). Declines like студент. Nominative: the ending is — (no ending).

exercises.q: Не столько его дерзость, сколько его ___ (позёрство, nom. sg.) бесит меня.
exercises.prompt: It's not so much his bragging as his posturing that bothers me.
exercises.why: **позёрство → позерство** (nom. sg.). Declines like окно. Nominative: the ending is -о.

exercises.q: ___ (остриё, nom. sg.) этого карандаша недостаточно острое.
exercises.prompt: The point of this pencil isn't sharp enough.
exercises.why: **остриё → острие** (nom. sg.). Neuter, nominative singular in -ие. Nominative: the ending is -е.

exercises.q: Том наставил свое ___ (ружьё, nom. sg.) на Мэри.
exercises.prompt: Tom pointed his gun at Mary.
exercises.why: **ружьё → ружье** (nom. sg.). Neuter, nominative singular in -е. Nominative: the ending is -е.
